claims.quote: α2δ-2 and GluK1, a glutamate-gated kainate receptor subtype, are coexpressed in cerebellar Purkinje cells.
α2δ-2 coexpression augmented GluK1, but not GluK2, currents in HEK293 cells
Pregabalin lost its inhibitory effect on GluK1 currents in HEK293 cells expressing both GluK1 and the α2δ-2(R282A) mutant.
α2δ-2, but not α2δ-1, formed a protein complex with GluK1 in cerebellar tissues and HEK293 cells through its C-terminus.
α2δ-2 coexpression potentiated surface expression of GluK1 proteins in HEK293 cells

Disrupting α2δ-2-GluK1 interactions using α2δ-2 C-terminus peptide abrogated the potentiating effect of α2δ-2 on GluK1 currents and attenuated the amplitude of GluK1-mediated excitatory post-synaptic currents in Purkinje cells.

claims.object_text: impaired beam-walking and rotarod performance in mice
claims.quote: CRISPR/Cas9-induced conditional knockdown of Cacna2d2 or Grik1 in Purkinje cells, in addition to microinjection of α2δ-2 C-terminus peptide or UBP310 into the cerebellum, substantially impaired beam-walking and rotarod performance in mice.
α2δ-2 directly interacts with GluK1 independently of its conventional role as a voltage-activated Ca2+ channel subunit.
α2δ-2 regulates motor coordination by promoting synaptic expression and activity in GluK1-containing kainate receptors in Purkinje cells.
